title: AI's bottomless pit problem: Investors are scrutinizing costs
excerpt: Investors are scrutinizing the AI trade amid concerns that companies may be throwing money into a bottomless pit.
content_html:
Nathan Bomey

Wed, August 5, 2026 at 2:57 PM PDT 2 min read

Investors are scrutinizing the AI trade amid concerns that companies may be throwing money into a bottomless pit.

Why it matters: Not all AI spending is created equal. Investors are drawing a harder line on companies that fail to show how today's AI investments will translate into profits.

  • "It's all about capex and free cash flow — and investors are not rewarding negative free cash flow," Melissa Otto, head of S&P Global's Visible Alpha Research, tells Axios in an email.

The big picture: The markets have punished several AI titans over AI capital expenditure concerns in recent days.

  • SpaceX plunged to new lows Wednesday, even after the company topped revenue expectations in Tuesday's earnings report, as investors fretted over its massive capex plans.

  • AMD shares slumped Wednesday despite a 50% jump in revenue as investors look for evidence that its customers' AI infrastructure investments will continue translating into accelerating returns, Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne tells Reuters.

  • Meta shares are down nearly $200 per share from their peak as the company continues to invest heavily in capex, having reported a 55% increase in expenses in its most recent quarter.

Zoom in: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk told investors on an earnings call Tuesday that the company now expects to reach $1 trillion in revenue by 2030, if not 2029, up from a previously projected 2031.

  • But his extensive commentary about the investments necessary to get there unnerved investors.

  • That includes rocket development, AI data centers, power deals — with compute capacity alone expected to hit 5 gigawatts to 10 gigawatts by the end of 2027, Musk said.

Yes, but: A strong cloud businesses could make a difference, the Wall Street Journal recently noted.

  • Amazon, Microsoft and Google have all rattled investors with eye-popping AI spending, but strong cloud results and massive backlogs of contracted demand have given their shares a recent boost.

The bottom line: "Investors have become increasingly discerning," according to Ed Yardeni, president and chief investment strategist of Yardeni Research.

  • "Instead of investing on faith, they've been assessing company by company whether future demand might be huge enough to justify the massive capex devoted to data center buildouts."

内森·博米

太平洋夏令时间 2026 年 8 月 5 日星期三下午 2:57 阅读 2 分钟

由于担心公司可能将资金投入无底洞，投资者正在密切关注人工智能行业。

为什么重要：并非所有人工智能支出都是平等的。 投资者对那些未能展示当今人工智能投资将如何转化为利润的公司采取了更强硬的态度。

  • 标准普尔全球 Visible Alpha 研究主管梅丽莎·奥托 (Melissa Otto) 在一封电子邮件中告诉 Axios：“这一切都与资本支出和自由现金流有关，而投资者不会奖励负的自由现金流。”

整体情况：最近几天，市场因人工智能资本支出担忧而惩罚了几家人工智能巨头。

  • 尽管该公司在周二的收益报告中超出了收入预期，但由于投资者对其巨额资本支出计划感到担忧，周三该公司股价仍跌至新低。
  • Emarketer 分析师 Jacob Bourne 告诉路透社，尽管收入增长了 50%，但 AMD 股价周三仍暴跌，因为投资者寻找证据表明其客户的人工智能基础设施投资将继续转化为加速回报。
  • 由于公司继续大力投资资本支出，Meta 股价较峰值每股下跌近 200 美元，最近一个季度的支出增加了 55%。

放大：SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在周二的财报电话会议上告诉投资者，该公司目前预计到 2030 年（如果不是 2029 年）收入将达到 1 万亿美元，高于此前预计的 2031 年。

  • 但他对实现这一目标所需投资的广泛评论让投资者感到不安。
  • 马斯克表示，这包括火箭开发、人工智能数据中心、电力交易——到 2027 年底，仅计算能力预计将达到 5 吉瓦到 10 吉瓦。

是的，但是：《华尔街日报》最近指出，强大的云业务可以带来改变。

  • 亚马逊、微软和谷歌都以令人瞠目结舌的人工智能支出让投资者感到不安，但强劲的云计算业绩和大量积压的合同需求使它们的股价最近得到提振。

底线：“投资者变得越来越挑剔，”亚德尼研究公司总裁兼首席投资策略师埃德·亚德尼表示。

  • “他们不是凭信心进行投资，而是一直在逐家评估未来的需求是否足以证明用于数据中心建设的巨额资本支出是合理的。”
